content.text: Digital creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and other regions face platform restrictions, forcing them to rely on unreliable payment infrastructure. When Stripe restricts access or PayPal is unavailable, digital stores are left without a payment layer. In this guide, we'll explore how to set up a Supabase order database for digital stores, a reliable alternative to conventional payment platforms. Supabase offers a free tier and scalable infrastructure, making it an ideal solution for digital creators who want to maintain control over their payment processing. With Supabase, you can deploy a digital store in 4-6 hours, using the Sovereign Blueprint, and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-start-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-complete-infrastructure|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-fonts-online-without-paypal-what-actually-how|Selling Fonts]]-digital-products-crypto-step-step-3|start]] processing transactions without relying on Stripe or PayPal.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Supabase order

The traditional payment infrastructure model relies on intermediaries like Stripe and PayPal, which can be restrictive and unreliable. When these platforms fail or are unavailable, digital stores are forced to shut down. In contrast, Supabase offers a self-hosted order database that allows digital creators to maintain control over their payment processing. By using Supabase, you can decouple your payment infrastructure from external platforms, ensuring that your digital store remains operational even when platforms fail.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying Supabase as your order database, you'll need to set up a GitHub Pages site and configure the payment and delivery pipeline using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. You'll also need to create a NOWPayments account and integrate it with your Supabase order database. Once you have these components in place, you can deploy your digital store using the Sovereign Blueprint and start processing transactions.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages to host your digital store, and then integrate it with Supabase using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. You'll also need to set up NOWPayments to handle payment processing and automatically trigger the delivery of digital products. This requires some technical expertise, but the Sovereign Blueprint provides a step-by-step guide to help you through the process.
Supabase offers a self-hosted order database that allows digital creators to decouple their payment infrastructure from external platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can deploy your digital store using the Sovereign Blueprint and start processing transactions. This typically takes 4-6 hours, depending on your technical expertise. You'll need to test your infrastructure to ensure that payments are being processed correctly and that digital products are being delivered as expected. With Supabase, you can also track sales and customer data in real-time, giving you valuable insights into your digital store's performance.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital store grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to handle increased traffic and transaction volumes. With Supabase, you can easily scale your order database to handle large volumes of data and maintain high performance. You can also integrate your digital store with other services, such as email marketing and analytics tools, to further enhance your infrastructure and improve your business operations.
How do I order by two columns in Supabase?

How do I order by two columns in Supabase? You can order by two columns in Supabase using the `ORDER BY` clause in your SQL query. For example, to order by the `created_at` column and then by the `id` column, you would use the following query: `SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC`. This will order your results by the `created_at` column in descending order, and then by the `id` column in ascending order.

Frequently Asked Questions
Is Supabase good for databases?

Yes, Supabase is a good database for digital stores because it offers a free tier and scalable infrastructure, making it an ideal solution for digital creators who want to maintain control over their payment processing. Supabase also provides a self-hosted order database that allows digital creators to decouple their payment infrastructure from external platforms.
How do I export Supabase database data?

To export Supabase database data, you can use the `SELECT *` query to retrieve all data from a table, and then use the `EXPORT` command to export the data to a CSV file. You can also use third-party tools, such as Supabase's own export feature, to export data in bulk.
Is Supabase free?

Yes, Supabase offers a free tier that includes 10,000 rows of data storage, 100,000 queries per day, and 10GB of storage. This makes it an ideal solution for small to medium-sized digital stores or startups that are just getting started.
Can I use Supabase with other services?

Yes, Supabase can be integrated with other services, such as email marketing and analytics tools, to further enhance your infrastructure and improve your business operations. You can use APIs, webhooks, or other integration methods to connect Supabase with other services.
How long does it take to deploy Supabase?
